page.title: Build with a coding agent · tinyactors
page.description: Connect a coding agent to the tinyactors support server for the guides, the skill for writing charts and known issues, and read every page of the site as Markdown.

hero.headline: Build with a coding agent
hero.lede: Your agent writes the charts; the support server gives it the guides, a skill for building with tinyactors and the known issues with their workarounds. Every page of this site is Markdown for it too.

section.heading: Connect the support server
section.p: An agent that guesses at an API it has not seen writes code that fails at the first run. The server at https://mcp.tinyactors.dev/mcp lets it read the packages' guides instead, and reading needs no account.
In Claude Code, claude mcp add registers it under the name tinyactors-support:
section.code: claude mcp add --transport http tinyactors-support https://mcp.tinyactors.dev/mcp
section.p: On claude.ai, add it under Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector, with the same URL. Any other agent that connects to MCP servers over HTTP takes that URL too.

section.heading: What your agent can do there

item.text: search_docs searches the packages' guides, and get_doc reads one whole.
Hosts with MCP's Skills extension list each skill as a skill:// resource; for the others, list_skills and get_skill read them.
known_issues lists the open issues, costliest first, with their workarounds, and get_issue reads one.
report_issue, attach_workaround and attach_file start a GitHub login the first time. Reports of the same problem become one issue, and the reporter hears when it changes.

section.p: Where the host renders MCP Apps, as Claude, ChatGPT and VS Code do, known_issues opens an issue list to filter, read and report from.

section.heading: The skill teaches your agent the workflow
section.p: The server's using-tinyactors skill says when a chart is worth its cost and how to build with one. Your agent reads it from the server, so there is nothing to install. Its workflow has five steps:

item.text: Decide which things are actors, who creates each kind, how they are named and how they end.
One .scxml file per kind of actor, every side effect a send to an I/O processor or an invoked service.

item.term: Make the host and its processors
item.text: One I/O processor per external system, such as a database or an HTTP client.
A SimulatedClock and a stand-in for every processor, so timeouts take no time.
Per kind of actor: a store with hibernation, snapshots of the whole host, or your own database.

section.p: A second skill, reporting-tinyactors-issues, has the agent look for a known issue before it reports one.

section.heading: Every page is Markdown too
section.p: Add index.md to a page's address for its Markdown, as in /guides/hibernation/index.md. /llms.txt lists every page, and /llms-full.txt holds every page but the changelog in one file.

section.heading: Why charts suit an agent
section.p: An actor reaches the world only through events. So an agent writes one from the events entering and leaving it, without reading the rest of your system.

A review of the agent's change reads one chart, where every state and transition is written down. In CI, tinyactors diff catches what a review can miss: here a renamed state that running orders still wait in.
Check charts in CI adds check, lint and diff to every pull request, so an agent's change that breaks a chart fails before anyone merges it.
